stops.note: 'near the kidneys', describing the adrenal glands on top of them

the Japanese chemist Jōkichi Takamine isolated the pure hormone in New York around 1900, and Parke-Davis trademarked it as Adrenalin in 1901; US medicine instead uses 'epinephrine', a name John Jacob Abel had coined in 1899
the standard British name, and 'adrenaline rush' for excitement dates from the later 1900s

current_meaning: a hormone released in stress that raises heart rate; excitement
